o.text:
Etymology tree
Proto-Semitic *ʔadam-
Biblical Hebrew אָדָם (āḏā́m)bor.
Arabic آدَم (ʔādam)bor.
Old Anatolian Turkish آدم (ādäm)
Azerbaijani adam
Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish آدم (ādäm), borrowed from Arabic آدَم (ʔādam).

From the causative form of Old Anatolian Turkish آلدامق (aldamaq, “to fool”), from Proto-Common Turkic *ālda- (“to deceive, fool”), a derivation from Proto-Common Turkic *āl (“craftiness; lie; strategy; way of doing”), whence also dialectal Azerbaijani al (“lie, untruth”).
Borrowed from Russian аудито́рия (auditórija), ultimately from Latin auditorium.
A derivation of Proto-Turkic *abï- + -t. Compare Old Uyghur 𐽰𐽰𐽱𐽶𐾀𐽹𐽰𐽲 (ʾʾvytmʾq, “to console a child; to spoil a child”).
